questions.q: What does the `packageDirectories` property in sfdx-project.json declare?
options: The list of users allowed to deploy to the org
An array of folders, each with a relative path, holding the project's deployable metadata
The scratch org's expiration duration
The CLI's installed plugin list
questions.explain: packageDirectories is a required array of objects, each with a path relative to the project root, declaring every folder that holds deployable metadata.

questions.q: If a project has only one entry in packageDirectories, what happens regarding the `default` flag?
options: You must still explicitly set "default": true on it
It's assumed to be the default automatically, with no explicit flag required
The project fails to build without a second entry
default only applies to packaged projects, never unpackaged ones
questions.explain: With a single packageDirectories entry, it's automatically treated as the default; the explicit default: true flag is only required to disambiguate when there are multiple entries.

options: Which version of Node.js the CLI requires
The Metadata API version that new metadata and source-format conversions target
The version number of the currently installed Salesforce CLI
The scratch org edition to use by default
questions.explain: sourceApiVersion determines which Metadata API version newly generated metadata and source conversions target — it affects which platform features a newly created component can actually use.

questions.q: What is `packageAliases` used for in sfdx-project.json?
options: Mapping human-readable package names to their internal package/package-version IDs
Listing aliases for every authenticated org the CLI knows about
Defining shortcuts for CLI commands
Storing a project's Git remote URLs
questions.explain: packageAliases is a generated map letting you refer to a package by a readable name (like "Expense Manager") in commands instead of its opaque internal ID, populated automatically as packages are created.

questions.q: A project has two entries in packageDirectories and neither is marked "default": true. What's the practical consequence?
options: Nothing — the CLI picks one at random each run with no issue
This violates the requirement that exactly one entry must be marked default when there's more than one package directory, so default-dependent operations like pulling changes have no clear target
The project automatically deletes the second directory
sfdx-project.json becomes read-only
questions.explain: With multiple package directories, exactly one must be explicitly marked default — it's the directory used for pulling org changes back in, source conversions with no explicit output, and default package creation. Omitting it leaves that ambiguous.
